Was in Jiankang during the murder. The crown prince made him General of the Right against Xinting, and he used that to join the loyal side. Xiaowu then made him Inspector of Sizhou, with command, and Administrator of Runan.

claims.unresolvedReason: Named only through ruined palaces. No year of his own life is given.
claims.event: The palaces Xiu burned are called his ruins. That later reference is not a year of his own life.
Of Guangping. Earlier he had been a Palace Guard general. In Yuanjia 27, helping defend Pengcheng, Wei forces captured him.
His acupuncture won Taiwu's regard. He was enfeoffed Duke of Nan'an, kept at Taiwu's side, and urged Xiu to defect.
His urging is what Xiu accepted before they came over in Yuanjia 28.
Sent with Shuang and Xiu toward Xu and Luoyang.
Attacked Qiaoao, failed, and withdrew. Shuang then also marched south. The fifth month is the one in the year after Yuanjia 28.
In Yuanjia 30 he murdered his father, Emperor Wen. He told Xiu he had killed Xu Zhanzhi for him, made Xiu General of the Right, and sent him against Xinting. The personal name is not in the text.

claims.statement: Told Xiu he had killed Xu Zhanzhi on Xiu's account and meant to trust him.

claims.event: Prince of Nanqiao. Raised troops against the crown prince. Shuang and Zang Zhi went to him at Jiangling.
Inspector of Yongzhou. Went with Shuang to Jiangling.

In Xiaojian 1, month 2, he conspired with Shuang to rebel and they agreed to rise in the autumn. Shuang rose at once. Yixuan then rose too. He was stunned by Shuang's commission naming him emperor and held the regalia at Jingling.
He sent Shuang out by Liyang. Later he and Zang Zhi were blocked at Liangshan, and he sent Liu Chenzhi and Zang Zhi against Wang Xuemo.
In Xiaojian 1, month 2, he conspired with Yixuan, rose the same day, had his men wear yellow insignia, and styled the year Jianping 1. Jianping is the era he proclaimed, not a separate calendar year.
He sent forged commissions to Jiangling. Yixuan held them at Jingling. Shuang was sent toward Liyang. Xue Andou met him, thrust him down, and the head was sent to Jiankang. Shouyang was then taken.

claims.statement: s0037 says Xue Andou killed Shuang with a thrust and forwarded the head. s0321 says Andou thrust him down, and s0322 says the attendant Fan Shuang cut off the head. Both are kept.
Commission naming Yixuan emperor, Zang Zhi chancellor, and Zhu Xiuzhi general of chariots and cavalry.

claims.event: Rose with Yixuan once Shuang had moved. Advanced by land and water. Shuang's commission named him chancellor. Later attacked Wang Xuemo at Liangshan and was routed.
Named in Shuang's commission as General Who Pacifies the West, to be made General of Chariots and Cavalry. Yixuan did not let the regalia proceed, so the new title was not carried out.

Of Fenyin in Hedong. His clan was a great house of some three thousand households, and his father Guang was its magnate. Andou was famous for valor from youth, seven feet eight inches tall, and skilled with bow and horse. In Wei he became overall commander of Yong and Qin. These precede his arrival in Yuanjia 21.

claims.statement: For generations a powerful clan, some three thousand households of the surname.
seven feet eight inches tall

label.en: overall commander of Yongzhou and Qinzhou

claims.event: In Yuanjia 21 he came over to Song, asked to return north, and stirred the Yellow River and Shaanxi. Emperor Wen agreed.
While Xiaowu held Xiangyang, between the Yuanjia 21 arrival and the year-27 campaign, Andou was made Administrator of Northern Hongnong, then fell back to Xiangyang as Wei grew stronger.

In Yuanjia 27 Prince Dan of Sui made him General Who Establishes Martial Might. He led Liu Yuanjing's infantry and cavalry toward the passes and Shaanxi and won each fight. At Jiukou he dreamed the Gate of Heaven opened.

When Xiaowu marched against the usurper, Andou led the cavalry with Liu Yuanjing. On the accession he became General of the Right Army, rode into the palace yard, and was enfeoffed Baron of Nanxiang. The year is Yuanjia 30 in the preceding units.
That year his cousin was beaten, he set out to kill Yu Shuzhi, Liu Yuanjing stopped him, and he was dismissed for bluntness.
In Xiaojian 1 he became General of the Left Army. Sent with Shen Qingzhi across the Yangzi, he rode at Lu Shuang and thrust him down. He was raised to marquis, then led a cavalry wing at Liangshan.

label.en: Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard

claims.event: In Daming 1 he led the cavalry toward Wuyan under Shen Tan, with Shen Faxi's fleet. The Wei army had gone. The pursuit of the Rencheng band failed in a drought. He and Faxi served in plain dress.
The next year, Daming 2, he was restored and re-enfeoffed Marquis of Wuchang.
In Jinghe 1 he became General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou, with overall command.

claims.statement: Asked his attendants whether they saw the Gate of Heaven open.
Said the dream of the Gate of Heaven opening was a sign of restoration.
Told Yuanjing he was going to kill Yu Shuzhi for beating his cousin.

claims.event: Andou's father and the clan magnate. When Emperor Wu took the passes and the river, Guang was made Administrator of Shangdang. No year is stated; it is before Andou's Yuanjia 21 arrival.
Took the passes and the middle Yellow River and appointed Guang to Shangdang. This chunk gives no year; it stands before Yuanjia 21.
Agreed to Andou's request, after the Yuanjia 21 defection, to go back north and stir the Yellow River and Shaanxi.
While stationed at Xiangyang, after Andou's Yuanjia 21 arrival and before the year-27 campaign, he commissioned Andou Administrator of Northern Hongnong.
Marched against the usurper with Andou and Liu Yuanjing leading the cavalry, then acceded. The preceding units place that accession in Yuanjia 30.
Xiaojian 1 is his era. In its second month Yixuan and Shuang rebelled.
Daming 1 is his era. He sent Andou and Shen Faxi under Shen Tan toward Wuyan.
In the twenty-seventh year, continuing Yuanjia, he commissioned Andou General Who Establishes Martial Might for the campaign with Liu Yuanjing.
Andou marched in his van toward the passes and Shaanxi in Yuanjia 27.
Set out with Andou when Xiaowu marched on the usurper. Later, at the Zhuque crossing, he talked Andou out of killing Yu Shuzhi.

claims.statement: Asked Andou where he was going, then rebuked him for meaning to kill in the capital.

claims.event: Andou's younger cousin. Won a Grand Marshal clerkship by military merit, then broke the law and was beaten by Yu Shuzhi. The beating is told after the accession, in the capital.
Magistrate of Moling. Beat Daosheng. Andou meant to kill him.
Sent with Andou across the Yangzi when Lu Shuang rebelled.
Andou's attendant. After Andou thrust Lu Shuang down, Fan Shuang cut off the head. s0037 instead credits Andou with forwarding the head.

claims.unresolvedReason: The comparison gives no year of this person's own life.
claims.event: People compared Andou's charge with Guan Yu killing Yan Liang. That is not a year of Guan Yu's life.

claims.action: said to have killed Yan Liang

claims.unresolvedReason: The comparison gives no year of this person's own life.
claims.event: Named only as the man Guan Yu killed in the comparison. No year of his own life is given.

claims.action: recalled as killed by Guan Yu

claims.event: Blocked Yixuan and Zang Zhi at Liangshan, ordered the assault, and sent Andou's cavalry into the enemy's right. The rebels broke.
Sent by Yixuan with Zang Zhi to attack Wang Xuemo at Liangshan. The attack was routed.
Administrator of Dongyang. In Daming 1 he led the fleet under Shen Tan. The English Faxing is 法系. After the failed pursuit he kept his post in plain dress.
Restored with Andou the year after Daming 1. The text says Andou was restored; Faxi had shared the plain-dress penalty.

Inspector of Xuzhou. Directed Andou and Shen Faxi in Daming 1. After the Wei army left, he was allowed to attack the Rencheng band. Drought stopped the pursuit, and he was imprisoned in the Shangfang.
Acceded, and Andou rose with Prince Zixun. The preceding unit is Jinghe 1, AD 465. He appointed Suo'er, sent the Qi founder north, and later had Fu Lingyue killed when he would not accept pardon.
When Ming acceded he rose with Zixun, recalled his nephew from the capital, and fled north with Liu Guangshi and his sons.

After Zixun was crushed he sent pledges of loyalty. The emperor then sent an army to receive him, and Andou, fearing punishment, yielded Pengcheng and defected to Wei. His clan went north. No later year is numbered.

Andou rose with him. He was Prince of Jin'an. In Jinghe 1 winter, after a poison envoy was sent, he came out in armor and the staff agreed to fight. The revolt was later crushed. The text does not say he died.
Andou's nephew, in the capital as General of the Left Army and a palace attendant. He fled north with Liu Guangshi and was later beheaded.
Right Guard General. Plotted with Andou and fled north with him. After Suo'er died he held Xiapi, then surrendered.
Inspector of Qingzhou. Rebelled together with Cui Daogu.
Inspector of Jizhou. Rebelled. His officer Fu Lingyue was captured at Shouyang. The English Dao Gu is 道固.
Emperor Ming sent him, with Zhang Yong, to suppress the northern rebels. Xue Suo'er was beheaded. The text already calls him Emperor Gao of Qi.
Acceded. Xue Shen, who had avoided Gao's partial name-taboo, was then made Administrator of Huaiyin. Gao's personal name is not written out.
Forward General under the Qi founder on the northern campaign.
Later sent with Shen Youzhi and a heavy army to receive Andou, which drove Andou to Wei.
General of the Martial Guard under Liu Mian, attacking Yin Yan at Shouyang. His men captured Fu Lingyue.
Wang Guangzhi's army was under him at Shouyang. He questioned Fu Lingyue and sent him to Jiankang.

claims.statement: Asked Lingyue why he had rebelled and why he had not come in to the court.

claims.event: Besieged at Shouyang by Liu Mian's force.
Cui Daogu's officer, from Qinghe. Captured, he refused to shift the blame and would not accept pardon, so he was killed.

claims.statement: Said he was Fu Lingyue, blamed Andou for trusting sons and nephews, and refused to beg for life.

claims.event: Andou's registrar. Carried the loyalty memorial to Emperor Ming after Zixun's revolt was crushed.
Administrator of Xiapi. Sent with Bi Zhong'ai.
Sent with Zhang Yong to receive Andou.
His crisis sent the Qi emperor into court. No numbered year is given; it falls between the close of Yuanhui and the Qi accession.
Andou's nephew. When Andou yielded Pengcheng the clan went north. While Gao held Huaiyin, Shen came south and attached himself to Gao.

claims.reason: avoided Emperor Gao of Qi's partial name-taboo

claims.event: By the close of Song's Yuanhui era he was General of Valiant Cavalry and a commander, and Marquis of Jingling. The English Yuanyuan is 元徽. No single year inside the era is stated.
During Shen Youzhi's crisis he held troops at the Minister of Works' right office, then answered Prince Yi and went to the rescue.
When Gao acceded, Shen became Administrator of Huaiyin, then Palace Guard General, then Left Leader of the Heir Apparent.

label.en: Left Leader of the Heir Apparent

claims.event: When Emperor Wu of Qi acceded, Shen became General of the Left Guard.
In Longchang 1 he became Inspector of Sizhou and General of the Right, and died.

claims.statement: resolute and physically strong

claims.event: During the crisis he held the Eastern Mansion for the Qi emperor and at night called Xue Shen from the western gate of Shitou.
Held Shitou. Prince Yi's call to Shen answered that seizure.
Acceded after Emperor Gao and moved Xue Shen to General of the Left Guard. This is the Qi emperor, not Song's Emperor Wu.

Courtesy name Yuanyan, of Nanchang in Yuzhang. When Xiaowu first rose, Wan was Administrator of Nanhai. Because his brother was banished with Zang Zhi, Wan stayed at Guangzhou. He later served as Assistant of Danyang. No year numeral is given; it is before Daming 7.
In Daming 7, when the emperor visited Liyang, Wan was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

label.en: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate

claims.event: The next year, Daming 8, he became Zixun's chief clerk and Interior Administrator of Xunyang, acting for Jiangzhou.
In Jinghe 1 the poison envoy's arrival was reported to him. He pledged to die for the trust Xiaowu had placed in him, and the staff then agreed to fight.

claims.statement: Said he was a poor southern scholar, entrusted by the late emperor with his beloved son, and would repay that with his life.

claims.event: Wan's father. Had been chief clerk to Xiaowu's General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Minister of the Imperial Household. No numbered year.

label.en: chief clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians

claims.event: When he first raised troops, Wan was at Nanhai. No year is numbered in this chunk; it is before Daming 7.
In Daming 7 he visited Liyang and promoted Wan.
The next year Wan was sent out to Zixun.
By Jinghe 1 Wan calls him the late emperor and the father who entrusted Zixun to him. The death year is not stated, only that he was already dead.
Wan's younger brother. Joined Zang Zhi's revolt and was banished, which kept Wan at Guangzhou.
Qiong joined his revolt. This chunk does not date that revolt except as before Daming 7.
Named, with Xiaowu, as a ruler who had come to the throne while third in the succession. No year of that remark is separate from the deposed emperor's suspicion.

Noted that Wen and Xiaowu had both reigned as the third son, suspected Zixun for the same rank, and, using He Mai's plan, sent poison. Zixun then took up arms instead. Jinghe 1 is the year of that winter.
His plan was the occasion for the poison sent to Zixun.
Zixun's registrar. Brought news of the poison envoy to Deng Wan.
Staff commander. Went with the registrar to Deng Wan.
Attendant scribe. Went with them to Deng Wan.
Recorder. When Zixun proposed to fight, Tao Liang offered to die in the van, and the rest agreed.

claims.statement: Asked to die in the van.

claims.event: While he was crushing the revolt he promoted Zixun, later sent generals against him, and refused officers who asked for promotion in the crisis. The numbered year in this chunk is Taishi 2.

claims.statement: Refused the requested posts: a loyal man does not bargain for reward in a crisis.

claims.event: On Taishi 2, month 1, day 7, he was enthroned at Xunyang. That same day the rebels renamed Jinghe 3 as Yijia 1. Jinghe 3 is their label for this year, not a separate western year.
Ming had promoted him to General of Chariots and Cavalry with a staff equal to the Three Excellencies. Wan rejected that and the officials hailed him emperor. Omens at the rite were read as ill.

label.en: staff equal to the Three Excellencies

claims.event: He threw Ming's order down, mustered troops with Tao Liang, raised a banner at Sangwei, and set a price on Ming. He had Gu Zhaozhi write the omen record, forged Chongxian's orders, and with his son sold offices. He sent Sun Chongzhi, Tao Liang, and Liu Hu.

claims.statement: Said Zixun should open the main palace gate, and that the Yellow Chamber was work for Wan's own sort.

claims.unresolvedReason: This chunk only compares him with Zixun and gives no year of his own life.
claims.event: Named only because Wan compared Zixun's rank and his rising at Xunyang with him.
With Wan he repaired arms and called up troops. He would not advance when Xiuren and Yin Xiaozu approached, and he refused Sun Chongzhi's plan to take the capital.
Inspector of Yingzhou. Joined the revolt and was named Minister of State, amid thunder that struck the Yellow Chamber pillar.
Inspector of Jingzhou. Joined the revolt.
Administrator of Kuaiji. Joined the revolt.
Inspector of Yongzhou. Wrote urging Wan not to disarm and telling Zixun to take the imperial title at once. 袁顗 is Yuan Yi; the English Yuan Yan splits the given name's sound.
Inspector of Liangzhou. Joined the revolt. 柳元怙 is Liu Yuanhu; the English Yuanku does not match 怙.
Inspector of Yizhou. Joined the revolt.
Inspector of Guangzhou. Joined the revolt.
Inspector of Xuzhou. Named in the list of those who rebelled.
Inspector of Qingzhou. Joined the revolt.
Inspector of Jizhou. Joined the revolt.
Acting head of Xiangzhou affairs. Joined the revolt.
Administrator of Wu. Joined the revolt.
Administrator of Wuxing. Joined the revolt.
Administrator of Jinling. Joined the revolt.
Administrator of Yixing. Joined the revolt.
Jingzhou registrar. Ming sent him by courier toward Jiangling, by way of Xiangyang.
Wan ordered him to compose the Record of the Auspicious Mandate.
Orders were forged in her name so the officials could hail Zixun. The text does not say she consented.
The father and son, Wan and this unnamed son, sold offices and titles and sent servants to trade in the streets.
Wan entrusted domestic business to Chu Lingsi and two unnamed others.
General Who Commands the Army. Led the fleet south against the rebels. Zhang Yong of Wuxing followed.
Administrator of Wuxing. Followed Wang Xuemo as the second force.
Held Zheqi with ten thousand men. He wrote asking to sail with the current to Baixia and for Tao Liang to take Xinting. The English says upstream; 沿流 is with the current.

claims.statement: Told Zixun to sail with the current for Baixia and asked Tao Liang to seize Xinting. After Xiaozu died he said the empire was already decided.

claims.event: Prince of Jian'an. Advanced from Wujian and took Zheqi. He had Chu Yanhui draft promotions, which the emperor refused.
Approached with Prince Xiuren. A stray arrow killed him, and Shen Youzhi replaced him in the van.
Took the van after Yin Xiaozu died. His side feared Liu Hu. He was rebuilding ships when Wan's planks drifted into his camp.
Gentleman Cavalier Attendant. Directed the loyal attack at Zheqi, which routed the rebels.
Inspector of Yuzhou, a veteran. Camped at Quewei. Countrymen under Shen Youzhi urged him to surrender; he drew back into Quewei and the fight stalled.
Liu Hu's countryman, under Shen Youzhi at Zheqi. With the others he urged Hu to come over.
Liu Hu's countryman, under Shen Youzhi at Zheqi.
Liu Hu's countryman, under Shen Youzhi at Zheqi.
Minister of Personnel. Ming sent him to Wujian to select officers. Xiuren had him draft a list the emperor rejected.
Asked for a Palace Attendant post while officers were being named at Wujian.
Asked, with Shen Qian, for a Palace Attendant post.
Asked for a Central Secretariat post.
Asked, with Shen Huaiming, for a Central Secretariat post.
General of Strong Crossbows. Brought reinforcing troops to Shen Youzhi.
Made Yuan Yi supreme commander. The ships that entered Quewei were Yuan Yi's. Wan later feared to send grain past Qianxi. Zhang Yue killed him.
Brought the fleet into Quewei, ordered Liu Hu against Zhang Xingshi, then fled west to Qinglin and was killed. 袁顗 is Yuan Yi.

label.en: supreme commander of the punitive army

claims.event: Urged holding Qianxi above Quewei to cut the grain route, and did so. Hu's attacks failed.
At Ming's accession he was made Commandant of Elite Cavalry. The Man feared even his name.
Failed against Qianxi, fled, was trapped by Chen Huaizhi, tried to stab himself, and was beheaded.

claims.reason: as an adult he was called by the single name Hu

claims.statement: sunken, dark face

claims.event: Led three hundred boats toward Qianxi under orders not to fight, and camped at Meigen instead.
Led a hundred boats against Zhang Xingshi and was badly beaten.
Ordered the Nonghu attack and later received Wan's head from Zhang Yue.
Attacked Nonghu and later beheaded Zixun at Sangwei.
Zong Yue confided the plot to him, and he told Ming. Yue and the others were killed that day.
Joined the attack on Nonghu.
Joined the attack on Nonghu.
Joined the attack on Nonghu.
Joined the attack on Nonghu.
In mourning for his nephew Hao, he trapped Wan, rejected selling the prince, and had his son Xun kill Wan. He took the head to Xiuren.

claims.statement: Asked whether Wan would sell the prince to save himself.

claims.unresolvedReason: This chunk gives no numbered year of this person's own life.
claims.event: Named only as the brother whose son Hao was. No year of his own life is given.

claims.unresolvedReason: This chunk gives no numbered year of this person's own life.
claims.event: Zhang Yue had begun his funeral. The text gives no year of Hao's life or death.
Wan and Yue discussed killing him. Cai Daoshen seized him, and Shen Youzhi beheaded him at Sangwei.
Zhang Yue's second son. He drew a sword and cut down Deng Wan.
His service to Ming is why his son Daoshen was chained. Daoshen then seized Zixun.
Broke his chains in the turmoil, entered the city, and seized Zixun.
The deposed emperor's southern tour let Yue sleep outside; Ming used that night to settle the court. He then had the plotters killed.

claims.statement: Offered Yue and the others any great military commandery they chose.

claims.event: Jingling assistant. Barred Liu Hu's road, brought him in, and was afterwards killed by Sengyan, who took Hu's head.

claims.unresolvedReason: This chunk gives no numbered year of this person's own life.
claims.event: Named only as Chen Huaizhi's father. No year of his own life is given.
Zhang Xingshi's brother. Killed Chen Huaizhi and falsely claimed Liu Hu's head.
After Nonghu fell, Jingzhou thought of taking him to Xiao Huikai. He was seized and surrendered.
Jingzhou debated fleeing to him in Yizhou with Prince Zixu.
Said, with Shao Zai, that flight west was impossible. They sent messengers to plead guilty.

claims.statement: Said that even if they still wanted the west, they could not get there.

claims.event: Joined Ruan Daoyu in refusing the flight west.
Led troops in with Yao Jian, seized Prince Zixu, and surrendered.
A local man. Entered the city with Zong Jing and seized Prince Zixu.

From Ye in Nanyang. Classed as a secondary household, then dropped to corvée while Zhao Lunzhi held Xiangyang. He avenged his father and Xiahou Mu made him platoon chief. This is before the Yuanjia 24 petition.
Asked Emperor Wen to restore his secondary-household rank and move his register to Guanjun. Wen agreed.
Joined Liu Yuanjing's invasion of Wei, served under Liu Yuanhu, and became a rear-army staff officer and protector. Prince Dan teased him. He said Foli was still alive.

On Xiaowu's accession he joined Prince Yigong's staff and became Administrator of Jiyang. In the Zang Zhi and Lu Shuang revolt he chased the enemy to Jiangling, abused Yixuan's children, was jailed, and was pardoned. He was then enfeoffed Viscount of Fanyang. No year numeral is given; it is before Daming 3.
In Daming 3 he became Commandant of the Long River.

Under Shen Qingzhi he attacked Prince Dan at Guangling. After the city fell he carried out Xiaowu's order and killed several thousand men. He was re-enfeoffed Viscount of Shi'an. The rebellion has no numbered year; it falls between Daming 3 and Jinghe 1.

In Jinghe 1 the deposed emperor made him a marquis, General of Mobile Strikes, and a palace guard, and he held Southern Jiyin, then Southern Donghai. He killed ministers and He Mai. After Ming's coup he plotted, was betrayed by Shen Youzhi, and was executed that day.

claims.statement: Told Prince Dan that while Foli lived he need not worry about failing to become a consultation staff officer.

claims.event: General Who Pacifies the North at Xiangyang. During his tenure Zong Yue was demoted to corvée status. No year is numbered; it is before Yuanjia 24.
Killed by the Man. Zong Yue killed that man in the market before the Yuanjia 24 petition.
Killed Zong Yue's father and was killed by Yue in the market.
Administrator. Made Zong Yue platoon chief for avenging his father.
Agreed to restore Zong Yue's secondary-household status and move the register to Guanjun.
Zong Yue joined his raid into Wei.
Zong Yue served under him with distinction. 柳元怙 is Liu Yuanhu, not Liu Yuanku.
Prince of Sui. Teased Zong Yue about the four-character post and laughed at the reply.

claims.statement: Asked Zong Yue who he was to earn a four-character post in the prince's command.

claims.event: As Prince of Jingling he rebelled at Guangling. Shen Qingzhi and Zong Yue attacked him. The year is not numbered.
Zong Yue said he was not yet dead, so Yue could still rise to consultation staff officer. 佛狸 is his name in the text. The English Buddha Li treats the transcription as the Buddha.
On his accession he appointed Zong Yue to Yigong's staff and to Jiyang. The year is not numbered here; it is before Daming 3.
After Guangling fell he ordered every male in the city killed. Zong Yue carried that out.
Grand marshal. Zong Yue served as acting clerk on his staff.
Rebelled with Lu Shuang. Zong Yue's merit in the pursuit was the greatest.
Rebelled with Zang Zhi.
Inspector of Jingzhou. Had not reached his post when Zong Yue was killing at Jiangling.
Prince of Nanjun. Zong Yue seized his sons and daughters. The English Nan drops the commandery.
Commanded the attack on Prince Dan at Guangling. Zong Yue's cavalry was under him.
In Jinghe 1 he promoted Zong Yue and used him, Tan Jin, and Tong Taiyi to kill ministers and He Mai. His night outside the palace let Ming move.
Served the deposed emperor with Zong Yue and was executed with him after the plot.
Served the deposed emperor with Zong Yue and was executed with him after the plot.
Killed by Zong Yue, Tan Jin, and Tong Taiyi.

claims.unresolvedReason: This chunk gives no numbered year of this person's own life.
claims.event: The camp anecdote and the soldiers' saying give him no numbered year.

claims.assessment: excelled at laying out camps, and was cruel and fond of executions

claims.unresolvedReason: This chunk gives no numbered year of this person's own life.
claims.event: The text says only that he had just died when Shen Youzhi took the van.
In Jinghe 1 the deposed emperor made him Baron of Dongxing. He had replaced Yin Xiaozu as southern vanguard and sighed that Lord Zong was a loss.

claims.statement: Said it was a pity about Lord Zong, who had his strengths.

claims.unresolvedReason: This chunk gives no numbered year of this person's own life.
claims.event: He appears only in the soldiers' saying, which gives no year.
In Wei he had known Xue Andou. After Andou came south, Jin campaigned as his deputy. That is before Xiaojian 3.
In Xiaojian 3 he was Commandant of Escort Cavalry, a palace guard, and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
In Jinghe 1 he served in the killing of the ministers and was made Baron of Pingdu.
Tan Jin knew him in Wei and, after he came south, served as his deputy.
In Jinghe 1 he slaughtered the ministers and enfeoffed Jin, Tong Taiyi, and Shen Youzhi.
Made Baron of Yiyang in Jinghe 1.

claims.unresolvedReason: The text gives his office but no numbered year.
claims.event: Became Administrator of Nanyang. No year is stated.

claims.unresolvedReason: The text gives his office but no numbered year.
claims.event: Became Commandant Who Pacifies the Man. No year is stated.

claims.unresolvedReason: The text gives his office but no numbered year.
claims.event: Became General of Valiant Cavalry. No year is stated.

claims.event: Named as a commander, with a pointer to his son Daogong's biography. No year is given.

claims.event: Named only so the reader will see his biography. No year of his life is given.
From Lin'an in Wuxing. His original name Xigong was shortened to Xi by Ming. At the accession he asked for three hundred men and was sent east.

label.en: acting General Who Establishes Martial Might

claims.event: In Taishi 4 he was re-enfeoffed Marquis of Dongxing and held the Right Army, Huaiyang, and the heir's left guard.

label.en: Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard

claims.event: In Taishi 5 he became General of Valiant Cavalry, keeping the other posts, and crushed Wei at Jingting.
In Taishi 6 he marched to Yuzhou against Wei with overall command.
The next year, Taishi 7, he returned to Jiankang.
After that return the text tells how Ming, once ill, doubted Xi would serve a young ruler and ordered him to die. No death year is numbered.

claims.statement: Told Ming that Wu Xi had served under Shen Qingzhi and would succeed if trusted.

claims.event: Shortened Wu Xi's name, sent him east, and later resented the sparing of Zifang.
When ill he ordered Wu Xi to die and forbade leaving the feast vessels in the house of death.

claims.unresolvedReason: His employment of Wu Xi is told with no numbered year.
claims.event: Had Xi copy the court diary and a lost memorial. No year is stated.

claims.unresolvedReason: The recommendation is told with no numbered year.
claims.event: Shen Yanzhi's student. Became Master of Documents and recommended Xi.

claims.unresolvedReason: These incidents are told with no numbered year.
claims.event: Dismissed Xi for presenting a book upside down, then allowed him to follow Shen Qingzhi.

claims.unresolvedReason: The Man campaign is told with no numbered year.
